title: Configuration Space and the Motion Planning Problem

contract.reader: An engineer or student who knows frames and the two-link arm from Introduction to Robotics and wants to know what planning a motion means before learning any planner
contract.problem: Turning "move this shape without hitting anything" into a precise problem, and knowing what a planner's answer or failure guarantees
contract.outcome: State a planning problem in configuration space; compute C-obstacles for a disk robot and numerically for the arm; explain topology, completeness and optimality; check an edge safely with a clearance bound; place the main planner families
contract.contribution: One worked thread (room with boxes, two-link arm and disk) carried from definition to C-obstacle area, a wall in joint space, components on the torus and a provable step bound, every number from runnable code
contract.evidence: Derivations, programs with real output, Lozano-Perez 1983, Schwartz and Sharir 1983, Reif 1979, Canny 1988, Gilbert et al. 1988, LaValle 2006 and others (numbers recomputed in the 2026-10-24 live review)
contract.limitations: Static obstacles, kinematic only; combinatorial planners named, not developed
